title: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) systems and maintenance
description: Louisiana Army National Guard is to replace its Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) systems and conduct maintenance in accordance with the attached PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS). The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and quality control necessary, except as specified in Paragraph 3.0 as Government Furnished, to perform Liebert and EATON UPS system maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair services, as defined in this PWS. In addition, the contractor shall install a 20KVA 480V INPUT 480V OUTPUT system with at least 10 MINUTE BATTERY capacity and the required batteries at the Jackson Barracks location, as specified in section 5.0.3.4. Proposals should include documentation from the manufacturer that you are qualified and certified to work on the items listed below. Vendors need to stock parts and/or have a relationship with the prime vendors that allows you to secure any necessary parts rapidly. Proposals should include documentation that you have access to OEM parts and will not provide cannibalized or used parts. Vendor must provide a certified letter from EATON and one from Liebert stating that their business is an authorized Third-Party vendor. Vendors must describe parts attainment process. What are the sources (EATON, Liebert, or cannibalized/older units)? Priority will be given to Authorized third party vendors who get parts directly from EATON and Liebert. Options may be exercised on some CLINs and not on others if that UPS is replaced or removed from inventory. Submission of a quote acknowledges receipt and understanding of the requirements; if there are any uncertainties about the requirements please ask prior to submission. title: Rough River LakeAxtel Wastewater Treatment Plant Replacement
description: Description of Proposed Work: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, anticipates issuing an Invitation for Bids (IFB) for a firm-fixed-price construction contract to execute the Rough River Lake Axtel Wastewater Treatment Plant Replacement. The overall scope of work comprises the complete demolition and decommissioning of the existing wastewater treatment plant and the construction of a new replacement subsurface sewage treatment and dispersal facility. Primary features of work include, but are not limited to:Demolition and Removal: Demolition and disposal of the existing Axtel Wastewater Treatment Plant, existing chain-link perimeter fencing, and gravel surfacing.Treatment and Disposal System Construction: Construction and installation of a new subsurface wastewater treatment and disposal system, including: Precast concrete primary pretreatment septic tanks conforming to ASTM C1227 and 902 KAR 10:081/085. Precast sewage lift stations, dose stations, and holding tanks. Packaged Aerobic Treatment Unit (ATU) / Advanced Wastewater Treatment System. Soil drip dispersal field and piping network.Piping and Distribution: Installation of gravity sewer piping and pressure piping networks, including supply/return manifolds, flush valves, and air release/vacuum breaker valves.Electrical and Control Systems: Complete electrical service and distribution, including coordination with Meade County RECC for service drop/upgrades, NEMA 4X (316 stainless steel) control enclosures, UL 1449 Type 2 Surge Protective Devices (TVSS), sequencing reactor controls, alarm systems, and associated conduits.Site and Civil Appurtenances: Rough and finish grading, trenching, erosion and sediment control measures, replacement chain-link perimeter security fence and gates with privacy slats, and site restoration.Optional Features: Contract Line Item Schedule includes an optional line item for Rock Excavation (unit-priced per cubic yard).

description: PROVISION FOR IT SUPPORT AND MAINTENANCE SERVICES FOR EHLANZENI DISTRICT MUNICIPALITY FOR A PERIOD OF THREE YEARS Tenders are hereby invited from capable and experienced service providers for the above-mentioned tender. 1. Only service providers who have provided the following mandatory information and documents to be used to evaluate the tenderer's responsiveness will be considered for further evaluation on functionality; 1.1 Only tenderers who are registered on the Central Supplier Database (CSD) will be considered and the copy of the full CSD report not older than three months should be submitted. 1.2 Form of offer must be firm, VAT and other tax inclusive and valid at least Ninety (90) days from the closing date. 1.3 No tender shall be considered for the person who are in the service of the state, 1.4 Valid SARS PIN certificate must be attached, 1.5 Attached original Certified copy of company registration documents issued by Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC). 1.6 Attached original Certified copies of Identity Documents (ID) of all company directors, 1.7 Attach verifiable Municipal Account/s not older than three months for both the tenderer and entity owner/s or director/s. In areas where the municipalities are not issuing municipal accounts, attach valid lease agreements or confirmation of residence or address for both the tenderer and entity owner/s or director/s issued by a relevant authority not older than three months. 1.8 Attached Valid letter from Department of Employment and Labour - COIDA registration letter, 1.9 Tenderers submitting tenders as a joint venture or consortium must attach a signed agreement by all parties to the joint venture or consortium. 1.10 Attach valid certified copy of COIDA Letter of Good Standing from the Department of Employment and Labour. 1.11 Attach audited or reviewed and signed Annual Financial Statements at least for the past three years. 1.12 Attach certified copies of ICASA ECNS and ECS License issued on your company name. 1.13 Attach audited and signed copies of audited Annual Financial Statements for the past three years since the company or since the company came into existence if not older than three years. 1.14 Fully completed tender document as issued and signed must be submitted on the PDF document that has been issued. All certified copies must not be older than three months. 1.15 Tenderers are advised not to commit any fraudulent activities, including forgery of documents. All abuses of the Supply Chain Management (SCM) systems including but not limited to forgery of returnable documents, may be reported to the South African Police Service (SAPS) and restricted from doing business with any public institution or organ of the state for a period not exceeding 10 years in line with the Prevention of Fraud and Corrupt Activities Act 12 of 2004. 2. This tender will be evaluated in accordance with the 80/20 preference point system in terms of the Preferential Procurement Policy of the Ehlanzeni District Municipality. The policy preference point system will be applied as follows; 2.1 The 80 points will be for price; and 2.2 The 20 points will be allocated for the specified goals on a proportional or pro rata basis as follows: POINTS FOR CONTRACTING AN ENTERPRISE OWNED BY HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED PERSONS OR INDIVIDUALS HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED PERSONS OR INDIVIDUALS POINTS ALLOCATION SOURCE DOCUMENTS REQUIRED TO CLAIM POINTS 100% black person or people owned Enterprise 3,00 A copy of a Full CSD report not older than 3 months More than 30% woman or women shareholding or owned enterprise 2,00 More than 30% youth shareholding or owned enterprise 2,00 More than 30% people living with disability shareholding or owned Enterprise 2,00 A copy of a Medical Certificate to confirm disability or stated on the CSD report More than 30% military veteran’s shareholding or owned Enterprise 2,00 A copy of a Full CSD report not older than 3 months POINTS FOR IMPLEMENTING OF RDP PROGRAMMES Enterprises regarded as *EME’s located within the Ehlanzeni District Municipality area of jurisdiction 2,00 ? A copy of a Full CSD report not older than 3 months NB: Points will only be awarded if the CSD physical address is the same as the address for the proof of residence required in 1.7 above. Sub-contract minimum of 30% of the contract value to EME’s in the ward or local communities where the services to be rendered of works to be undertaken 2,00 ? Commitment letter of works or services to be sub-contracted. Corporate Social Investment (CSI) or Social Labour Plan proposition 3,00 ? Attach a CSI plan or Social Labour Plan B-BBEE level 1 contribution 2,00 ? Certified Valid SANAS Accredited BBBEE certificate; or ? Certified Valid EME and SME a sworn affidavit; or ? Certified Valid CIPC issued certificate confirming annual turnover and level of Black Ownership. TOTAL PREFERENCE POINTS TO CLAIMED 20,0 *EME’s are Exempted Micro Enterprise with an annual turnover of R10 million or less. Received tenders will be evaluated for responsiveness based on mandatory requirements, functionality and tenderers who obtain a minimum of 70 points out of a possible 100 points, will be further evaluated on price and specified goals. Tender documents can be viewed and downloaded at no cost on the Document Sharing and Collaboration Platform or Portal (NEPTUNE): http://edmservices.ehlanzeni.gov.za and National Treasury Portal from Wednesday, 26 August 2026. Further information regarding the downloading and uploading of documents will be explained at the compulsory briefing session. A compulsory briefing session will be held on Wednesday, 02 September 2026, 10h00 at Ehlanzeni District Municipality Office Complex, DMC, 8 Van Niekerk Street, Sonheuwel Central, Mbombela, 1201. title: Imaging of Southern Nova Scotia coastline using ShoreZone methodologies
description: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) requires coastal imaging services in support of the Canadian Coast Guard's Area Response Planning (ARP) initiative under the Oceans Protection Plan (OPP) 2.0. The objective of this project is to apply imaging methodologies consistent with the ShoreZone Coastal Imaging and Habitat Mapping Protocol (Cook et al., 2017) to expand existing coastal habitat datasets in southern Nova Scotia. The work will involve the acquisition of coastal imagery and video data along approximately 1,750 km of Nova Scotia coastline, beginning near Lobster Bay and extending northward toward Halifax. The resulting data will support oil spill preparedness, planning, and response activities by improving the availability of geographically specific coastal habitat information. Contractors must conduct all imaging and video collection in accordance with the ShoreZone Coastal Imaging and Habitat Mapping Protocol and the requirements specified in the solicitation documents. Complete details of the requirement are contained in the Request for Proposal (RFP) documents.

title: Leiri- ja kurssikeskusvaraukset
description: Kesälukioseura järjestää Suomessa asuville pakolaislapsille ja -nuorille leirimuotoisia oman äidinkielen ja kulttuurin kursseja. Kesälukioseura etsii vuoden 2027 kursseja varten leiri- ja kurssikeskuksia eri puolilta Suomea. Kurssit ajoittuvat koulujen loma-ajoille (talvilomaviikko 8, kesä–heinäkuu). Oman äidinkielen ja kulttuurin kursseja järjestetään 8–9 (1–2 talvella, seitsemän kesällä). Kesän kurssit ovat pituudeltaan vajaan viikon mittaisia (5 vrk, esim. ma–la). Talvilomaleirin kesto on 4 vrk, ma-pe. Kursseille osallistuu noin 20–32 iältään 7–14-vuotiasta lasta sekä 4–7 omakielistä opettajaa. Jokaiselle osallistujalle pitää olla leirin aikana vuodepaikka (ei patjamajoitusta). Kesälukioseura vastaa kurssien järjestämisestä. Kurssien ohjaajatiimit vastaavat kurssien opetuksesta ja ohjelmasta. Kurssien järjestämisestä aiheutuvat kulut katetaan sosiaali- ja terveysministeriön myöntämällä avustuksella. Avustusta haetaan vuosittain, ja vuoden 2027 avustuspäätös selviää alkuvuodesta 2027. Hankinnan vertailuperusteina ovat turvallisuus, kokonaisedullisuus, luonnonläheisyys, kulkuyhteydet, riittävät opetus- ja harrastetilat, majoitus ja ylläpito sekä ajankohta. Tarjouksen voi tehdä yhdestä tai useammasta kurssiviikosta. Tarjouksesta tulee käydä ilmi ajankohta, jota tarjous koskee.

title: Tikkurilan terveys- ja sosiaalikeskuksen lisäpohjatutkimuksen hankinta
description: Tikkurilan terveys- ja sosiaalikeskuksen lisäpohjatutkimuksen hankinta Hankinnan kohteena ovat Tikkurilan uuden terveys- ja sosiaalikeskuksen tontille toteutettavat lisäpohjatutkimukset, joilla täydennetään vuosina 2020–2021 tehtyjä pohjatutkimuksia. Tutkimusten tavoitteena on täydentää hankkeen lähtötietoja, vähentää maaperäolosuhteisiin liittyviä epävarmuuksia sekä tukea kilpailullisen neuvottelumenettelyn aikana tarjoajien suunnittelua ja runkoratkaisujen arviointia. Lisätutkimuksilla tarkennetaan erityisesti maaperän pilaantuneisuutta (PIMA), savikerrosten geoteknisiä ominaisuuksia sekä kallionpinnan ja kallioperän sijaintia. Palvelu sisältää tutkimusten suunnittelun, kenttätutkimusten toteuttamisen sekä tutkimusaineiston toimittamisen tilaajalle sovitussa muodossa. Tutkimukset sisältävät mm. kairauksia, näytteenottoa, pohjavesihavaintoja ja muita geoteknisiä maaperätutkimuksia. Palvelu sisältää myös tarjouspyynnössä edellytettyjen tutkimusten, analyysien ja tutkimusraporttien laatimisen. Tutkimusten tavoitteena on täydentää hankkeen lähtötietoja, vähentää maaperäolosuhteisiin liittyviä epävarmuuksia sekä tukea kilpailullisen neuvottelumenettelyn aikana tarjoajien suunnittelua ja runkoratkaisujen arviointia. Lisätutkimuksilla tarkennetaan erityisesti maaperän pilaantuneisuutta (PIMA), savikerrosten geoteknisiä ominaisuuksia sekä kallionpinnan ja kallioperän sijaintia. Tutkimustulosten hankekokonaisuuden tasoisesta tulkinnasta sekä jatkosuunnittelua tukevista geoteknisistä johtopäätöksistä vastaa tilaajan konsultti. Nyt hankittavien lisäpohjatutkimuksien tavoitteena on varmistaa hankkeen riskienhallinnan ja jatkosuunnittelun tueksi luotettava ja yhtenäinen lähtötietopohja, joka julkaistaan kaikille neuvotteluvaiheessa mukana oleville tarjoajille Hankintayksikkö valitsee yhden (1) toimittajan, jonka kanssa se tekee sopimuksen. Kilpailutuksen perusteella valitaan myös yksi (1) varatoimittaja, jonka kanssa voidaan solmia varsinainen sopimus, mikäli sopimustoimittaja ei täytä sopimuskauden alkaessa tarjouspyynnön ehtoja ja edellytyksiä, tai mikäli sopimustoimittaja ei täytä näitä ehtoja ja edellytyksiä sopimuskauden aikana. Kyseessä on kertahankinta. Hankinnan arvioitu arvo n. 60 000 euroa,

title: Greece – Transport agency services – Παροχή υπηρεσιών μεταφοράς έργων τέχνης της έκθεσης με θέμα «Νικηφόρος Λύτρας»
description: Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης είναι η παροχή υπηρεσιών μεταφορών έργων τέχνης και ειδικότερα συσκευασία, μεταφορά και ανάρτηση έργων της περιοδικής έκθεσης με θέμα «Νικηφόρος Λύτρας». Αναλυτικότερα, οι υπηρεσίες παρέχονται σε δύο (2) φάσεις: Φάση Α1. Εγκατάσταση της περιοδικής έκθεση με θέμα: «Νικηφόρος Λύτρας» στο χώρο των περιοδικών εκθέσεων, στο επίπεδο -2 του κεντρικού κτιρίου της ΕΠΜΑΣ που βρίσκεται στο επίπεδο -2 του Α΄κτιρίου Η εγκατάσταση θα υλοποιηθεί τους μήνες Νοέμβριο – Δεκέμβριο 2026. Περιλαμβάνονται ενέργειες συντονισμού παραλαβής έργων τέχνης από φυσικά ή νομικά πρόσωπα που δανείζουν τα έργα τους στην αναθέτουσα αρχή, συσκευασίας, παραλαβής, μεταφοράς και ανάρτησης/ εγκατάστασης έργων τέχνης εντός και εκτός του νομού Αττικής και εκτός Ελλάδος μετακίνησης έργων τέχνης μεταξύ των εγκαταστάσεων της αναθέτουσας αρχής στην Αττική, μεταφοράς έργων τέχνης από παράρτημα της αναθέτουσας αρχής εκτός του νομού Αττικής, όπως και τοποθέτησης ή μετακίνησης υάλινων προπετασμάτων προθηκών καθώς και μετακίνησης προθηκών ή αντικειμένων που σχετίζονται με την έκθεση. Φάση Α2. Απεγκατάσταση της περιοδικής έκθεσης με Θέμα «Νικηφόρος Λύτρας» από χώρο των περιοδικών εκθέσεων στο κτίριο της Εθνικής Πινακοθήκης – Μουσείο Αλεξάνδρου Σούτσου . Περιλαμβάνονται ενέργειες, συντονισμού παράδοσης έργων τέχνης, αποανάρτησης/ απεγκατάστασης συσκευασίας και μεταφοράς/ παράδοσης έργων τέχνης στα φυσικά ή νομικά πρόσωπα (εντός και εκτός Αττικής και εκτός Ελλάδος), που έχουν δανείσει έργα τους για να συμμετάσχουν στην έκθεση με θέμα «Νικηφόρος Λύτρα», καθώς και α) εσωτερικές μεταφορές έργων τέχνης των συλλογών της αναθέτουσας αρχής εντός του κτιριακού συγκροτήματος που διεξάγεται η έκθεση, β) μεταφορές στις εγκαταστάσεις της αναθέτουσας αρχής στην Αττική, γ) μεταφορές έργων τέχνης σε παράρτημα της Αναθέτουσας Αρχής εκτός του νομού Αττικης (Σπάρτη), καθώς και γ) εκ νέου ανάρτηση έργων τέχνης στους χώρους των μονίμων συλλογών της αναθέτουσας αρχής. Η απεγκατάσταση θα υλοποιηθεί τον Οκτώβριο του 2027.

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Obtain Clinical Cohort of Patients with Associated Clinical Outcomes, Radiologic Images, and Associated De-Identified Radiology Reports
description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Thomas Jefferson University to Obtain Clinical Cohort of Patients with Associated Clinical Outcomes, Radiologic Images, and Associated De-Identified Radiology Reports. In accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, The requested clinical cohorts, radiographic imaging datasets, clinical outcomes data, and de-identified radiology reports are required to support artificial intelligence-based research focused on evaluating liver cancer risk in patients with cirrhosis and indeterminate liver lesions. The research requires datasets that combine specific patient populations with associated imaging studies and clinical outcomes information to enable the development, validation, and evaluation of predictive models. Alternative datasets that do not include the required patient populations, imaging data, clinical outcomes information, and associated radiology reports would not provide the information necessary to support the approved research objectives. The absence of any of these data elements would limit the ability to correlate imaging findings with clinical outcomes and would reduce the scientific validity and reliability of the resulting analyses. Therefore, only datasets containing the required clinical cohorts and associated imaging and outcomes data will satisfy the Government's minimum needs and support the approved research objectives. The objectives of the maintenance agreement are as follows: The objective of this requirement is to acquire clinical patient cohorts, associated imaging data, clinical outcomes data, and de-identified radiology reports to support the development and evaluation of A.I. models for liver disease and liver cancer research conducted by the Liver Diseases Branch. A determination by the Government to compete this proposed acquisition based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The proposed contractor maintains an existing cohort of patients with cirrhosis and associated radiographic images collected at six-month intervals, as well as an existing cohort of patients with cirrhosis and indeterminate liver lesions, including associated clinical outcomes data and radiographic images. These clinical cohorts and associated datasets represent a unique research resource available through the proposed contractor. The combination of longitudinal imaging data, clinical outcomes data, and radiographic images associated with these patient populations is available only through the proposed contractor. As a result, only the proposed contractor can provide the requested deliverables necessary to support the research project. It is anticipated that an award will be issued approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another vendor has the capability to meet this requirement. Please submit responses electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 25, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01240 in the subject line of the response.

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Doric Lenses FluoPulse Fiber Photometry / Fluorescence Lifetime Photometry System and Accessories
description: FAR 6.302-1 � Only One Responsible Source Solicitation Number 75N98026Q01219 Title Doric Lenses FluoPulse Fiber Photometry / Fluorescence Lifetime Photometry System and Accessories Description of Requirement The National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA), SensMET, requires an integrated fiber photometry and fluorescence lifetime photometry system to support ongoing and planned intramural research experiments. The requirement will support neuroscience research experiments that require time-resolved, two-color photometry recordings, optogenetic stimulation capability, calibrated optical power measurement, synchronized behavioral video acquisition, and compatible data analysis software. The National Institutes of Health, National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA), intends to award a contract to Government Scientific Source, Inc. on a sole-source basis pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, for the acquisition of a Doric Lenses FluoPulse Fiber Photometry / Fluorescence Lifetime Photometry System. Doric Lenses FluoPulse Fiber Photometry / Fluorescence Lifetime Photometry System and Accessories Pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, the Government intends to solicit and award a Purchase Order on a sole-source basis because the Government's minimum technical requirements will be satisfied by Government Scientific Source, Inc. Accordingly, the Government intends to award a sole-source contract to Government Scientific Source, Inc. pursuant to FAR 6.302-1. The requiring activity needs an integrated fluorescence lifetime photometry/fiber photometry platform for intramural neuroscience research experiments requiring two-color photometry recording, optogenetic stimulation capability, calibrated optical power measurement, synchronized behavior video acquisition, and compatible data analysis software. The requested Doric FluoPulse configuration includes a FluoPulse console; a seven-port fluorescence lifetime photometry recording mini cube with two integrated photodetectors, two integrated laser diode/excitation channels, an external 560 nm laser port, 500-540 nm and 580-600 nm detection paths, and 638 nm opto capability; a compatible fiberoptic rotary joint and low-autofluorescence fiber interfaces; a 638 nm, 80 mW laser diode fiber light source; a power meter package; a USB 3.0 behavior camera; a calibration sample; a Doric-configured high-performance workstation; and one-year danse data analysis software license. These components are requested as an integrated system because the optical hardware, fiber interfaces, calibration components, workstation, camera, and software must operate together as a validated experimental workflow. A substitute or piecemeal system would require redesign and revalidation of the optical path, fiber connections, calibration procedure, acquisition settings, and data analysis workflow, creating technical risk and potentially delaying or interrupting intramural research experiments. The requested supply/service therefore meets the Government's need for a complete, compatible, manufacturer-supported FluoPulse system configured for two-color + opto single-site experiments. Government Scientific Source Inc. is the quoted distributor/source for the Doric FluoPulse console, fluorescence lifetime photometry mini cube, Doric-compatible fiberoptic accessories, FluoPulse calibration sample, Doric-configured workstation, and danse data analysis software license. Government Scientific Source Inc. is positioned to provide the complete integrated package under one order, including manufacturer-compatible hardware, software, accessories, calibration components, shipping/handling, and DDP customs clearance. Because compatibility among the console, mini cube, fiberoptic components, laser/light source, power meter, camera, workstation, calibration sample, and analysis software is essential to successful experimental performance, a third-party or mixed-source solution would not provide the same manufacturer-supported configuration and would introduce unacceptable risk to system compatibility, setup, calibration, and technical support. Accordingly, the proposed contractor is capable of providing the requested integrated supply/service as quoted. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required supplies and meet all specified technical and operational requirements. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 25, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01219 in the subject line of the response.

description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Alongside Aircraft Refueling Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Cannon, AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates issuing one solicitation and awarding four (4) firm fixed-price contracts for Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. These requirements will be for a four-year base period (December 01, 2026 � November 30, 2030), a five-year option period (December 01, 2030 � November 30, 2035), and a option to extend the contract s for up to six individual months (December 01, 2035 � May 31, 2036).This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. description: Service for � BD FACSDiscover S8 BRVYGUV (SN: R66515800038) Maintenance Contract Notice No.: 75N98026Q01241 The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to BD Biosciences for a BD FACSDiscover S8 BRVYGUV (SN: R66515800038) Maintenance Contract. In accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, The National Institutes of Health (NIH) is the nation's medical research agency, and the mission of the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) is to support research on arthritis, musculoskeletal, and skin diseases through scientific discovery, training, and dissemination of research findings. The NIAMS Flow Cytometry Section (FCS) provides centralized flow cytometry and cell sorting services to investigators within the NIAMS Intramural Research Program and collaborating NIH researchers. The FCS operates several cell sorters, including the BD FACSAria Fusion, BD FACSMelody, Cytek Aurora CS, and the BD FACSDiscover� S8 Cell Sorter (Serial No. R66515800038). The BD FACSDiscover� S8 is the only instrument in the FCS that combines full-spectrum flow cytometry with real-time, camera-free imaging, enabling simultaneous fluorescence, spatial, and morphological analysis during cell sorting. These unique capabilities improve identification of target cell populations, enhance sort quality and purity, and support advanced applications that cannot be performed on the Section's other cell sorters. The instrument is a critical resource supporting ongoing NIH intramural research and has been used in numerous studies, including muscle stem cell isolation for the NIAMS Laboratory of Muscle Stem Cells and Gene Regulation, where its imaging technology has improved sorting efficiency and post-sort purity. The objectives of the maintenance agreement are as follows: The NIAMS Flow Cytometry Section (FCS) seeks to acquire a maintenance service contract for the BD FACSDiscover S8 BRVYGUV (SN: R66515800038). The primary objective of this procurement is to ensure the continued operation and reliability of flow cytometry services that support NIAMS intramural research. Maintaining this instrument under a comprehensive service agreement will help ensure optimal performance, minimize downtime, and sustain the high level of functionality required to support ongoing research efforts. A determination by the Government to compete this proposed acquisition based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. It is anticipated that an award will be issued approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another vendor has the capability to meet this requirement. title: Helium Reliquifiers for NMR Magnet
description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Institutes of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), intends to award a contract to Bluefors Cryocooler Technologies, Inc. on a sole-source basis pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, for the acquisition of Helium Reliquifiers for NMR Magnets , the Government intends to solicit and award a Purchase Order on a sole-source basis because the Government's minimum technical requirements will be satisfied by Bluefors Cryocooler Technologies, Inc. The Solid State NMR and Biomolecular Physics Section (SSNMRBP) of the Laboratory of Chemical Physics (LCP), National Institutes of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) uses nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy to investigate the molecular structures, motions, and interactions of biomedically relevant protein assemblies, including amyloid fibrils involved in neurodegenerative diseases, viral capsid assemblies, and proteins from nuclear pores of eukaryotic cells. NMR measurements are performed in powerful magnets. These magnets must be cooled with liquid helium to maintain high electrical currents in the superconducting materials within the magnets. Since the liquid helium in the NMR magnets continuously vaporizes ("boils off"), the liquid helium must be refilled periodically. Prices of liquid helium have increased dramatically over the past 20 years and liquid helium deliveries are frequently unreliable due to worldwide political events and conflicts. Increased prices and unreliable delivery threatens to require that NMR magnets be shut down. This would bring research projects in SSNMRBP to a halt. Helium recycling for the NMR magnets in SSNMRBP therefore has paramount importance. The Cryomech division of Bluefors Cryocooler Technologies, Inc. has recently developed "helium reliquifier" systems that can be attached directly to NMR magnets, allowing the NMR magnets to be operated continuously without helium refills. The helium reliquifier system recycles helium by capturing helium gas that exits from the magnet, compressing and cooling the helium gas to form liquid helium, and returning the liquid helium directly into the magnet. Two NMR magnets are used for most research in SSNMRBP, namely a 141 kilogauss magnet in room B2A-04 of building 8 on the NIH campus in Bethesda and a 175 kilogauss magnet in room B2-33 of building 5. Each of these two magnets requires its own helium reliquifier system. Two helium reliquifier systems are required. One system must be compatible with the dimensions of a 175 kilogauss NMR magnet manufactured by the Magnex company, located in room B2-33 of building 5 on the NIH campus in Bethesda, MD. The other system must be compatible with the dimensions of a 141 kilogauss NMR magnet manufactured by Oxford Instruments, located in room B2A-04 of building 8 on the NIH campus in Bethesda, MD. Each helium reliquifier system must be capable of generating at least 3 liters per hour of liquid helium on a continual basis, using helium gas that exits the NMR magnet due to evaporation of liquid helium within the magnet. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required supplies and meet all specified technical and operational requirements. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 25, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01223 in the subject line of the response.

title: Performance Assurance Services
description: The Marine Corps Logistics Command intends to award a sole-source contract to Phillips Corporation, Federal Division, for Performance Assurance, preventive maintenance, inspection, testing, and related maintenance support services for Government-owned industrial manufacturing equipment located at Production Plant Barstow, Yermo Annex, Yermo, California. Phillips Corporation, Federal Division, is the only authorized source capable of providing Performance Assurance services for the Haas and OMAX equipment covered by this requirement. The Government�s current intent is to include additional equipment manufactured by companies other than Haas and OMAX under the same contract for contract-administration convenience, coordinated scheduling, continuity of service, centralized accountability, and mitigation of performance and operational risks. The anticipated scope includes scheduled Performance Assurance services, preventive maintenance, equipment inspections, functional assessments, calibration analysis, vibration analysis, geometry inspections, Renishaw ballbar testing, drawbar force testing, OMAX annual waterjet services, replacement of specifically included maintenance components, equipment-condition reporting, and recommendations for follow-on corrective maintenance or spare parts. The requirement covers Government-owned industrial machines manufactured by Haas, OMAX, LVD/Strippit, Cincinnati, Fadal, Trumpf, Hyundai-Kia Machine, and Hardinge. The anticipated contract will include a base period and option periods. The Government does not intend to issue or post a solicitation for the Haas and OMAX portion of this requirement because Phillips Corporation, Federal Division, is the only authorized source for the required Performance Assurance services. However, before making a final acquisition determination, the Government is conducting market research to determine whether qualified sources exist to service the covered equipment manufactured by companies other than Haas and OMAX and whether separating that portion of the requirement would be in the Government�s best interest. This notice is not a request for quotations or proposals. Responsible sources may submit capability statements addressing only their ability to provide Performance Assurance services for the covered equipment manufactured by companies other than Haas and OMAX. Responses concerning the Haas and OMAX equipment are not requested. Capability statements must clearly demonstrate the firm�s ability to: Service the applicable equipment manufactured by LVD/Strippit, Cincinnati, Fadal, Trumpf, Hyundai-Kia Machine, and Hardinge; Identify the specific manufacturers, equipment models, and services the firm is capable of supporting; Provide qualified personnel with applicable OEM training, certifications, authorizations, or demonstrated experience; Perform the required preventive maintenance, inspections, functional testing, condition assessments, and reporting; Provide all required labor, supervision, tools, diagnostic equipment, travel, maintenance components, and technical expertise; and Meet applicable OEM requirements, manufacturer-recommended maintenance practices, and technician qualification requirements. Interested sources must submit their capability statements electronically to GySgt Matthew Radi at matthew.radi@usmc.mil no later than 25 September 2026 at 9:00 am EDT Submissions must include, at a minimum: Company name and address; Unique Entity Identifier and CAGE Code; Business size and applicable socioeconomic status; Point of contact information; Specific manufacturers and equipment models the firm can service; Applicable OEM authorizations, certifications, or technician qualifications; Relevant experience performing similar services; and Sufficient technical information for the Government to evaluate the firm�s capability. The Government will use the information received solely for acquisition-planning and market-research purposes, including determining whether it is in the Government�s best interest to separate the non-Haas and non-OMAX equipment from the contemplated Phillips sole-source contract. If the Government determines that separating the requirement is not practicable or in its best interest, it may proceed with an integrated sole-source award to Phillips Corporation, Federal Division. A determination regarding whether to separate any portion of the requirement is solely within the Government�s discretion. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a capability statement. The Government is not obligated to acknowledge responses, conduct discussions, or award a contract as a result of this notice.

Urinalysis sample collection for offenders This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Barrie, Ontario Trade agreement: This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement to provide Urinalysis Collection Services for male offenders in Barrie and the surrounding geographical area. The work will involve the following: 1.1 Objectives: Consistent with the Mission Statement and Strategic Objectives of the Correctional Service of Canada (CSC), the contractor must provide a Urinalysis Collection Program for the Barrie area extending to the surrounding rural areas. 1.2 Tasks: 1.2.1 The Contractor must: 1. Upon referral, collect urine samples from federally released male offenders. 2. Provide a collector that must be of the same gender as the offender providing the sample. 3. Accurately label, store and package samples to prevent contamination or tampering. 4. Record necessary information, including time of collection, collector identification, and complete other required documentation. 5. Explain the urinalysis process clearly to offenders, maintaining a calm and respectful demeanor. 6. Handle potentially sensitive or uncomfortable situations with discretion and empathy. 7. Ensure the integrity of the sample by placing the required seals on the container, obtain signatures on the container, and prepare the container for shipment to the specified laboratory for testing. 8. Ship the samples with a bill of lading to the approved laboratory for testing. 9. Collect samples in compliance with Section 66(1) of the CCRA regulations, and CD 566/566-11. The contractor must provide protective gloves to the collectors. 10. Present the offender with form 1064-1 (Community Notification to Provide a Urine Sample) prior to the initial test or at the beginning of a new frequency of urine collection if CSC requests one, obtain the offender’s signature, complete the Chain of Custody Form 1065 for every sample collected and distribute copies of the form as directed. 11. Complete the urinalysis log sheets monthly, or provide a detailed invoice, or both, and forward them to the respective office responsible for the supervision of the offender. 12. Attend court hearings, meetings with auditors, or meet with CSC managers as requested. 13. For all cases assessed by CSC to meet the tandem supervision policy, the contractor must provide a collector and an additional member of its staff or a person approved by the project authority who must accompany the collector whenever a urine sample is collected in the offender's private residence or in an isolated community location (CD 715). CSC will brief both the collector and the additional member of the contractor's staff or approved person on safety concerns. 14. Immediately notify the CSC supervising parole office if the collector notes that an offender refuses or is unable to provide a sample, or displays any suspicious behaviour, or both. If this occurs outside the contractor’s established working schedule, the contractor must follow the National Monitoring Centre protocol. 1.2.2 Collection Schedule: 1. Normally, the contractor must perform collections during regular working hours, Monday to Friday, between 0700 hours and 1800 hours. 2. CSC may request that the contractor collect urine samples, from time to time, on weekends and after normal working hours. 3. CSC may request that the contractor collect urine samples on an emergency basis. The contractor must respond within 3 to 4 hours of being notified of an emergency requirement. 4. The contractor must respond within 24 hours’ notice for any non urgent requests to schedule collection. 1.2.3 Continuity of Services 1. The collector must provide 24 hours’ notice for cancellation of collections. The contractor must provide this notice to the Office Urinalysis Coordinator. 2. The contractor must provide a back-up for urinalysis collection, in case of illness, vacation, leave, or the inability to provide urinalysis collection services for at least 5 days. description: VOORAANKONDIGING EUROPESE OPENBARE AANBESTEDING Dit betreft een vooraankondiging waarmee de gemeente Rotterdam de markt vroegtijdig wil informeren over een aankomende opdracht, nog vóórdat de eigenlijke aanbestedingsprocedure formeel van start gaat, zodat geinteresserde ondernemers zich kunnen voorbereiden. Bij een vooraankondiging kunnen partijen zich nog niet aanmelden, nog niet inschrijven, nog geen vragen stellen of formele aanbestedingsdocumentatie inzien. De werkelijke inschrijving kan pas zodra de officiële aanbesteding wordt gepubliceerd. De Bosdreef wordt in twee fasen naar het noorden verlegd om ruimte te maken voor de nieuwe woonwijk Nieuw Kralingen en een bedrijvenstrook. Fase 1 is opgeleverd in 2024. Op of omstreeks 19 juni 2026 wordt de Europese openbare aanbesteding gepubliceerd voor de opgave van fase 2. Het doel van de Opdracht van fase 2 is de realisatie van fase 2 van de Verlegde Bosdreef als volwaardige noordelijke ontsluitingsroute (1x2-baansweg, 50 km/u) ter vervanging van de huidige Bosdreef (thans 2x2-baansweg, 70 km/u). De beoogde startdatum van de werkzaamheden in deze Opdracht fase 2 staat gepland op 1 februari 2027. De Opdracht die in de Europese openbare aanbestedingsprocedure zal worden beschreven gaat over: Nieuw wegtracé (50 km/u-gebiedsontsluitingsweg) met fundering, verharding, markering en wegmeubilair Compleet rioleringssysteem (hemel- en vuilwater) aansluitend op bestaande infrastructuur Operationele VRI's en openbare verlichting Nieuwe, bredere betonnen Crooswijksebrug (niet-beweegbaar) Geïntegreerd infrastructuursysteem Volledige verbinding tussen fase 1 en fase 2 Vergunningen, keuringen, opleverdocumentatie en overdracht aan beheer (RAW-systematiek) Het werk bestaat in hoofdzaak uit : Grondwerk (ontgraven en ophogen inclusief verwerken) Het slopen van een betonnen brug (inclusief fundatie) Het bouwen van een betonnen brug (inclusief fundatie) Het aanbrengen van en grondkering (stalen damwand met verankering) Verwijderen asfaltverharding Aanbrengen asfaltverharding inclusief fundering Aanbrengen elementenverharding inclusief fundering Aanbrengen / installeren van een gemaal Aanleg DIT-riolering / riolering Aanleg persleiding Aanleg waterberging Aanleg verkeersregelinstallaties Aanleg installatie openbare verlichting Bijkomende werkzaamheden De bovenstaande opsomming van werkzaamheden is slechts een indicatie van de te verrichten werkzaamheden en alleen bedoeld om de interesse van potentiële Inschrijvers voor de Europese openbare aanbestedingsprocedure te wekken. Inschrijvers kunnen geen rechten ontlenen aan deze opsomming. Zie voor een nadere technische omschrijving van de uit te voeren werkzaamheden de aanbestedingsleidraad en het daarbij gevoegde RAW-bestek zoals dat op of omstreeks 19 juni 2026 zal worden gepubliceerd via dit Aanbestedingsplatform.

title: Netherlands – Medical software development services – Digitaal Dossier Jeugdgezondheidszorg
description: De aanbestedende dienst doorloopt een Europese aanbestedingsprocedure om een robuust en toekomstbestendig DDJGZ te selecteren en implementeren. Het systeem moet volledig operationeel en gebruiksklaar worden opgeleverd. Het DDJGZ moet voldoen aan de gestelde functionele en technische eisen en duurzaam zijn ingericht. De opdracht betreft de levering, implementatie en het beheer van een SaaS‑applicatie (DDJGZ) ten behoeve van de Jeugdgezondheidszorg. De scope omvat configuratie, datamigratie, koppelingen met relevante externe systemen, opleiding van gebruikers en doorlopend beheer en support. Het systeem moet beschikbaar zijn voor circa 230 medewerkers en geschikt zijn voor opschaling. De overeenkomst heeft een looptijd van 10 jaar inclusief optionele verlengingen.

title: France – Site preparation work – Réalisation des travaux préparatoires à l’extension d’une installation nucléaire existante
description: Le CEA projette la construction d’un bâtiment d’extension d’une installation existante sur le centre de Valduc. Afin de garantir la parfaite préparation de l’emplacement retenu, le CEA souhaite, à travers le marché objet de ce présent avis, réaliser les travaux préparatoires nécessaires à l’aménagement de la zone de construction. Ces travaux correspondent aux prestations suivantes : - L’aménagement de la zone de chantier ; - La dépose et le dévoiement de réseaux existants sur la zone ; - Le réaménagement du merlon situé sur le bâtiment adjacent au futur bâtiment, y compris la dépose d’ouvrages existants ; - La réalisation de la plateforme du futur bâtiment et des futures bases vies pour la phase travaux ; - L’évacuation sur le site des matériaux de déblais excédentaires ; - L’amenée de tous les réseaux nécessaires (dont Eaux Usées, Eaux Industriels, Eau Potable, Infrastructures pour Courants Forts et Courants Faibles Industriels). Les travaux du présent Marché correspondent aux travaux préparatoires préalables à la construction d’une extension d’un Bâtiment existant. Ces travaux comprennent en part ferme : • La zone d’installation chantier du Titulaire, y compris signalisation de chantier, • La réalisation des éléments assurant la délimitation de la future zone chantier qui comprend : o L’implantation des limitations des futurs ouvrages o La mise en place de clôtures et de barrières de protection o La réalisation de la plateforme et des sujétions associées au futur poste de gardiennage, y compris réseaux secs et humides • La dépose et/ou dévoiement de réseaux secs et humides (dont EP, EI, AEP, CFO, CFI,) • Le réaménagement du merlon du bâtiment existant avec les sujétions associées dont notamment : o La dépose du merlon (environ 7500m3) o La dépose d’ouvrages d’existants en béton armé (ouvrages de soutènement et galerie extérieure) o La réalisation de nouveaux ouvrages de soutènement en béton armé pour le merlon en toiture sur 50ml environ o La mise en bardage du voile extérieur du bâtiment existant, y compris toutes sujétions (60m x 12m environ) • L’aménagement de la plateforme de la future extension (environ 1500 m3 de déblai) (profondeur d’environ 1m) • L’aménagement de la zone des bases vie pour une surface approximative de 1300m² • L’évacuation des matériaux de déblai (zone de dépose sur le site à 1.5 km en aller simple) • La mise en place des réseaux, postes et équipements électriques pour le futur chantier depuis le bâtiment existant (1 armoire de distribution générale de chantier alimentant les bases vie, les grues et les coffrets de chantier) • La mise en place des arrivées de réseaux secs et humides pour les futures bases vies de chantier • La dépose et l’évacuation du poste électrique HT/BT existant et présent sur l’emprise chantier ainsi que les structures associées, y compris liaisons électriques • Un suivi géotechnique de type mission G3 • La pose de candélabres sur poteau bois avec haut-parleurs (environ une dizaine) • L’établissement de tous les documents nécessaires à la bonne exécution des travaux (études d’exécution, documents d’organisation de chantier...) mentionnés supra • La réalisation des contrôles et essais à réaliser pour les postes mentionnés supra • Le dossier des ouvrages exécutés Les prestations optionnelles à réaliser au titre du marché sont décrites infra. Les prestations prévues au BPU vont notamment concerner les domaines suivants : • Le détour d’un camion de terre de déblais par l’entrée du centre de Valduc pour contrôle radiologique (distance 6km en aller simple) • L’évacuation sur le site des matériaux de déblais excédentaires • Un arrêt de chantier d’un jour • Un arrêt de chantier d’une semaine ouvrée NOTA 1 : cette liste de prestations prévues au BPU n’est pas exhaustive. NOTA 2 : Les volumes précisés supra correspondent à des quantités estimées par le CEA. Elles ne constituent pas un engagement du CEA. Les prestations optionnelles du marché sont les suivantes : • L’agrandissement du bassin d’orage (130m3 maximum) • Alimentation des bases vie depuis un futur poste HT BT (hors périmètre de ce marché) (environ 200ml) Les prestations se déroulent sur le Centre CEA/DAM de VALDUC en Zone Protégée avec contraintes d’accès et d’exploitation.

title: REPAIR LIVE FIRE TRAINING FACILITY AIRCRAFT MOCK-UP
description: Amendment 0003-SOW/Specification Change The 910th Airlift Wing requires repair and corrective work to the Aircraft Fire Training Facility (AFTF) aircraft mock-up located at Youngstown Air Reserve Station. An inspection and evaluation of the Aircraft Fire Training Facility was conducted in August 2025 and finalized in April 2026. The assessment identified deficiencies affecting the facility's burner and ignition systems, structural components, corrosion protection, sprinkler system, propane distribution and emergency shutoff systems, control systems, and associated components. The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, testing, quality control, and other items and services necessary to complete the work identified in the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and solicitation attachments. Troubleshooting, repair, and/or replacement of the Tail Engine Burner, Wheel Well Burner, Flight Deck Burner, and Cargo Area Burner and associated ignition systems. Repair or replacement of burner ignition components as required to restore proper operation. Replacement of the malfunctioning cargo-area sprinkler head and restoration of proper drainage functionality. Structural steel repairs and corrosion remediation beneath portions of the aircraft mock-up. Corrosion repair beneath flight-deck stairs and around door assemblies. Repair and/or replacement of the warped R2 door and warped grating near the cargo-fire area. Certified welding and associated aircraft mock-up repairs. Installation/restoration of an emergency energy shutoff capability at the propane storage area. Installation of required solenoid valve(s) in the LPG/propane distribution system. Correction of deficiencies involving legacy pneumatic shutoff valves. Required control-system repairs/upgrades. Associated maintenance, testing, and corrective actions necessary to provide a complete and functional system. Applicable standards identified in the Government's technical documentation include, as applicable: USAF Technical Order 35E1-2-13-1 NFPA 54 NFPA 58 NFPA 70 NFPA 1003 NFPA 1402

title: Rees Scientific Database Migration and Software Upgrade
description: Rees Scientific Database Migration and Software Upgrade Acquisition No.: 26-009527 NAICS Code: � Other Computer Related Services PSC Code: DA01 � IT and Telecom � Business Application/Application Development Support Services (Labor) The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Clinical Center (CC), Office of Purchasing and Contracts, on behalf of the Department of Transfusion Medicine (DTM), intends to award a firm-fixed-price purchase order to Rees Scientific, 1007 Whitehead Road Extension, Trenton, NJ 08638, on a limited-source basis for database migration and software upgrade services. The purpose of this acquisition is to migrate the existing Rees Scientific database to new servers currently in the possession of NIH Information Technology (IT) and upgrade the Rees application software to a current supported version. The requirement is identified as Rees Build Version 3.0 Build 2601. Rees Scientific currently provides the environmental monitoring system used by the Department of Transfusion Medicine to monitor regulated environments, including room temperature, humidity, refrigerators, and freezers. The system supports DTM operations subject to applicable regulatory requirements, including requirements under 21 CFR and 42 CFR. Rees Scientific is the sole-source provider for the proprietary database migration and software upgrade required under this acquisition. The database migration and software upgrade are required by the manufacturer to ensure continued support of the database and Rees software application. The requirement also supports operational continuity of the existing environmental monitoring system. The Rees system is used within regulated environments supporting patient care, blood product manufacturing, and clinical laboratory diagnostic activities. Continued availability and proper operation of the environmental monitoring system are necessary to maintain the safety and quality of these operations. The Government has determined that Rees Scientific possesses the proprietary capability necessary to migrate the existing Rees database and upgrade the associated application software. Based on the information currently available to the Government, no other source is known to be capable of meeting the Government's requirements for the proprietary Rees database and software. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, all responsible sources that believe they can satisfy the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement and supporting documentation demonstrating their ability to provide the required proprietary Rees Scientific database migration and software upgrade services. Responses must include sufficient information to demonstrate the respondent's ability and authorization to perform the required services on the existing Rees Scientific system without compromising system functionality, regulatory compliance, warranties, or operational continuity. Interested parties shall submit capability statements electronically to the shasheshe.goolsby@nih.gov by September 25, 2026 at 10:00AMEST.

title: Market Intelligence Notice: Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station Taxiway A4 & Runway Extension Project - Use of Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) Utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE Place of Performance: Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station (NFARS), New York Notice: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 237310 � Highway, Street and Bridge Construction. (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction to extend Runway 10-28 and associated taxiways at the Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station, New York. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver fully functional airfield improvements. The primary project elements include: a. Reconstructing the existing overrun/blast pad on Runway 28 end to full-strength airfield pavement. b. Extending Runway 10-28 and extending Taxiway A4 to connect the 914th ARW apron to the new Runway 28 end. c. Extending a 520-foot portion of Runway 6-24 and providing a warmup pad for two (2) KC-135R aircraft. The potential total area of new airfield pavement is approximately 780,000 sq ft. d. Modifying the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Medium-Intensity Approach Lighting System with Runway End Identification Lights (MALSR) approach lighting, which requires active coordination with FAA construction representatives during removal and re-installation. e. Installing new airfield electrical and lighting systems, including runway edge lights, runway centerline lights, threshold lights, touchdown zone lights, airfield signage, and taxiway edge lights. f. Constructing a new creek culvert to allow the new taxiway to traverse the Cayuga Creek. g. Erecting a jet blast deflector fence on the Runway 28 end. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $50,000,000.00 CRITICAL PROJECT CONSTRAINTS & CHALLENGES: Geotechnical Constraints: The project site features variable and shallow bedrock (as shallow as 3 feet below grade) and a high groundwater table that heavily complicates subdrainage and stormwater design. Sensitive Environmental Conditions: Work will occur near federal and state-regulated wetlands and Cayuga Creek. The site is a habitat for the Devil Crayfish, which is listed as a species of Greatest Conservation Needs. Multiple permits with State and Federal agencies will be required prior to construction. Operational Constraints: A significant portion of the work will occur within the active runway Controlled Movement Area (CMA). Work requires compliance with an FAA-approved Construction Safety and Phasing Plan (CSPP), temporary displaced threshold markings, modifications to NAVAIDS, and FAA flight checks. Security Constraints: Strict security constraints are in place, requiring Government escorts at all times during construction. Airfield Pavement Quality Control: Onsite batch plant space (approx. 6 acres) has been identified. Review and final approval of concrete and asphalt mix designs reside with the USACE Transportation Service Center (TSC). The TSC will provide a mandatory, weeklong airfield pavement workshop prior to the start of construction, which the contractor�s key personnel must attend. Stakeholder Coordination: The contract requires active coordination with the airport operator (Niagara Frontier Transportation Authority - NFTA), USACE, Air Force Reserve Command (AFRC), FAA, and Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station (NFARS). PLANNED ACQUISITION STRATEGIES UNDER EVALUATION: Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. Currently, the Government has advanced the design to 35% and has the capability to progress to a full design. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The CM@Risk Course of Action (10 U.S.C. � 2808a): This Course of Action utilizes the 10 U.S.C. � 2808a OT authority to execute a construction project where the design is at 35% completion. Phase 1 Preconstruction: The builder is hired during Phase 1 to act as an expert consultant, helping the Designer of Record (DOR) push the design from 35% to 100% using real-time market data and MII (MCACES 2nd Generation) cost comparisons. Phase 2 Construction: Once the design hits 100% and the MII estimate validates the open-book pricing, the agreement transitions to Phase 2, where the builder goes "At-Risk" to construct the facility under a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). The DOR retains design liability, but the contractor drives constructability and assumes responsibility for layout, schedule, and trade coordination. The CM@Risk Pricing Structure: Preconstruction Services Fee: A small, fixed-price or time-and-materials amount paid to the contractor strictly to fund their time spent helping the Architect Engineer (A/E) finalize the 35% design into a 100% design. The Target Fee: The contractor�s transparent profit margin for managing the actual construction, bid competitively upfront. The GMP: The absolute ceiling for the construction phase (Validated Direct Costs + Target Fee + Shared Contingency). PHASED EXECUTION PLAN Phase 1: Preconstruction Services Agreement (CM@Risk Advisory) Solicitation (White Papers): The Solicitation would likely include the 35% design. The Deliverable is anticipated to be a concise 5-10 page White Paper. Evaluation Criteria will likely include Corporate capability and experience with collaborative project delivery methods ( including CM@Risk, Progressive Design-Build (PDB) and/or Design-Build to Budget (DBtB)) under an OT framework; preconstruction approach (how the firm plans to collaborate with the Government's A/E to close the remaining 65% design gap, identify value-engineering opportunities, and mitigate supply-chain risks); proposed Target Fee (for construction) and Preconstruction Services Fee. The Pitch Meeting (Oral Presentations): A 90-minute pitch where the contractor must bring their Project Manager, Site Superintendent, and their Preconstruction Manager. The Government team assesses how well the contractor's team will integrate with the A/E during the critical final design push. The OT is initially awarded and funded only for the Preconstruction Services Fee. Design Finalization (Bridging the 65% Gap): The contractor�s Preconstruction team sits with the Government and the DOR. Because the design is not locked, they can actively change it. They perform value engineering, finalize equipment selections, and ensure the drawings are 100% constructible. title: Guatemala – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Asistencia Técnica para la implementación de la Agenda de inversiones Global Gateway en Guatemala – Global Gateway Facility Guatemala
description: En 2021, la Comisión Europea lanzó la estrategia de inversiones Global Gateway, que tiene como objetivo fomentar inversiones de gran calibre en infraestructura verde y digital en los países socios, con soluciones innovadoras y de calidad, creando al mismo tiempo valor añadido local y promoviendo el crecimiento económico, el empleo y la cohesión social. Durante la III Cumbre UE-CELAC, celebrada en julio de 2023, los dirigentes de ambas regiones reafirmaron su compromiso de reforzar la asociación birregional, reconociendo la importancia de la Agenda de Inversiones Global Gateway. Dicho compromiso fue renovado durante la IV Cumbre UE-CELAC celebrada en noviembre de 2025. El objetivo general de esta acción es contribuir a la implementación de inversiones sostenibles y transformadoras en los sectores de transición verde y digital en Guatemala, donde haya un interés común europeo y de la agenda de desarrollo de Guatemala, y ello en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway, asegurando su alineación con las prioridades estratégicas del país y fomentando un desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible. La Asistencia Técnica contribuirá a: mejorar la alineación, coordinación y monitoreo de las iniciativas implementadas en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway en Guatemala; promover un marco regulatorio e institucional que favorezca la inversión sostenible en los sectores prioritarios de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway; impulsar proyectos de inversión sostenibles, transformadores y sensibles a la igualdad de género y a las buenas prácticas internacionales en materia de derechos y protección del medioambiente en los sectores prioritarios y a posicionar los intereses del sector privado europeo en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway para Guatemala. Sin excluir otras potenciales áreas de trabajo prioritarias para la UE y Guatemala, y reconociendo la flexibilidad dinámica de la estrategia Global Gateway, las áreas prioritarias para Guatemala actualmente incluyen transición verde (transporte sostenible, energía renovable e integración eléctrica regional, economía circular, gestión sostenible de recursos naturales y residuos) y transición digital (conectividad, gobernanza digital, ciberseguridad, innovación digital, observación de la Tierra, inteligencia artificial).

description: The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is a Cabinet-level executive branch department of the Federal Government whose workforce is comprised of approximately 650,000 clinical and non-clinical personnel (of which approximately 450,000 are employees) charged with providing lifelong healthcare services to eligible military veterans at the 1,380 health care facilities, including 170 VA medical centers and 1,193 outpatient sites located throughout the country. Non-healthcare benefits include disability compensation, vocational rehabilitation, education assistance, home loans, and life insurance. The VA also provides burial and memorial benefits to eligible veterans and family members at the 157 VA managed or 125 VA grant-funded cemeteries. VA employs a highly skilled and multi-faceted workforce aligned with its mission, program, and operational needs. Workforce Development is one of the key factors to recruiting and retaining a high-performing workforce. VA employs individuals at every competency and skill level whether they are new to the workforce or experts in their occupation. That said, VA workforce needs differ at every career stage. VA Federal personnel are encouraged annually to complete My Development Plans (MDP). They work with supervisors to determine short and long- term career goals as well as short-term training needs. Training needs are then documented on the MDP. The VA�s Leadership Development Framework (LDF) is based on the Federal-wide United States Office of Personnel Management Executive Core Qualifications. By using the VA LDF, VA personnel will be better able to assess their leadership capabilities for developmental purposes and to support the Department�s workforce, talent development, and succession planning efforts. Certain VA Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices require its workforce to complete technical competency assessments and leadership competency assessments for non-supervisory positions. VA personnel will complete leadership and technical competency assessments through the Department�s Talent Management System (TMS) 2.0 or Learning Management system of record (LMS). VA personnel must also meet certain training requirements throughout the year. These requirements may be prescribed as Federal Mandatory Training such as No Fear Act, Information Security Awareness, Occupational Health, and Safety, or Telework. Some personnel must complete training required by their occupation or role such as Cyber security role-based training. VA personnel access most of their training through Talent Management System TMS 2.0. This platform provides a common LMS and learning content services that enable VA to maximize the return on taxpayer investment. TMS 2.0 has a robust and secure environment to accommodate approximately 450,000 end users, ~12,000 administrators and over 500 unique domains. TMS 2.0 is the Department-wide system for managing training records and activities at VA. The purpose of this contract is to acquire eContent, Digital Books, Professional Development Training and Support Services to meet the training requirement of VA.
